facts.value: Argos Holdings Inc. (Parent) and Argos Merger Sub Inc., BC Partners-affiliated. At closing Parent is owned by the Buyer Group: funds advised by BC Partners, La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec, GIC Special Investments affiliates, StepStone Group affiliates and (after 12/12/2014) Longview Asset Management.
Financial (private-equity-led consortium with institutional co-investors and a rolling shareholder)
$83.00 per share in cash. Longview contributes 3,012,050 shares (about $250 million) to Parent instead of cash and receives $83.00 cash on its other shares.

Undated: PetSmart “from time to time” received inquiries about its interest in a sale (p. 21). Q1–spring 2014: the board considered merging with or acquiring Industry Participant, a privately held rival. In March 2014 it authorized contact, and the CEOs spoke in spring 2014 and over the next two months. Industry Participant said it was not for sale and raised antitrust concerns (p. 21). PetSmart was the potential buyer, so this is not a sale process.

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices

facts.value: J.P. Morgan Securities LLC (retained July 2014); an unnamed financial advisor attended the 06/18/2014 board meeting

After a weak first quarter, activists JANA Partners (9.9%) and Longview pressed PetSmart to sell in mid-2014. On 08/13/2014 the board decided to explore a sale and announced it on 08/19, refusing to admit a strategic rival, Industry Participant, on antitrust grounds. Of 27 parties that contacted J.P. Morgan, 15 financial buyers signed confidentiality and standstill agreements, and six submitted preliminary indications on 10/30. On 11/03 the board sent the four at or above $80 to a final round, where two of them combined as Bidder 3. At the 12/10 final-bid deadline the Buyer Group bid $80.70 and Bidder 2 $80.35, while Bidder 3 valued the company no higher than the market price. After a request to improve, Bidder 2 bid $81.50 and the BC Partners-led Buyer Group, now working with Longview on a rollover, bid $83.00 in cash, and the merger agreement was signed on 12/14/2014.

cells.Question: Process and round map: one process with two rounds (round 1 opened 08/19/2014, round 2 opened 11/03/2014), plus round 0 before the announcement and post after signing. Is this map right?
cells.Recommended answer: Keep one process and two rounds. Round 1 opens with the 08/19 announcement, which the 08/13 decision designed as the solicitation. Round 2 is the announced “final round” from 11/03; the 12/10 request to improve continues it.
cells.Why, with page: Alternatives: (i) round 1 opens at the first-week-of-October NDAs (p. 23), putting #9 and #11–#13 in round 0; (ii) the 12/10 request (p. 25) opens round 3, moving #37–#46. Gaps: none of about two months or more with no acquirer contact from 08/07 to signing. E5: (a) not met (activity continuous); (b) not met (no break reported or of about three months); (c) met only by the 08/13 decision, which starts process 1. The spring 2014 Industry Participant talks were about PetSmart combining with or buying a rival, and are undated beyond “Spring”, so they get no process.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Under (i), Industry Participant’s refusal and the 27 contacts leave round 1, which then starts with 15 entrants and no earlier contacts. Under (ii), round 2 stays Announced as final but its 12/10 outcome becomes Enforced, and a round 3 (Announced as final) holds the 12/12 bids, selection and signing.

cells.Recommended answer: Late bids accepted. Bidder 2 raised its indication from $78.00 to $81.00–$84.00 after the due date (10/30–11/02 calls), and the board counted it among the four at or above $80.00 on 11/03.
cells.Why, with page: p. 24: “As a result of its discussions with J.P. Morgan … increased its indication”; the board allowed “the four bidders that had indicated a price or range at or above $80.00”.
cells.What changes if answered differently: If the revision is seen as a clarification of a timely bid, the outcome is Enforced. Either way the Bid row stands, and Bidder 2’s admission to round 2 depends on its late revision.

cells.Question: Round 2 deadline outcomes: 12/05 → 12/10 → 12/12. Is 12/05 superseded, and what happened at 12/10 and 12/12?
cells.Recommended answer: Mark 12/05 “superseded before arrival”: the committee changed it on 12/04–12/05 and no bids were expected that day. Mark 12/10 Extended (improved bids requested for 12/12 in the same round) and 12/12 Enforced (board acted on 12/13).
cells.Why, with page: p. 24–25: “had initially set Friday, December 5”, revised “on December 4 and December 5”; p. 25: “submit improved bids on December 12”; p. 26: the 12/13 board reviewed “the final bids”.
cells.What changes if answered differently: If the 12/05 change came after that date had passed, 12/05 needs a Deadline row with outcome Extended. If 12/10 opens a new round (Q1 alternative ii), the 12/10 outcome becomes Enforced.

cells.Question: Who formed Bidder 3, and why does the Reasons section count 5 IOI “bidder groups” when the Background counts six submitters?
cells.Recommended answer: Treat Bidder 3 as Unnamed financial bidders 1 and 2, both admitted to round 2. That leaves three finalist groups, matching the December bidders, and makes the six IOIs five groups after combination.
cells.Why, with page: p. 24: one partner “had been invited into the final round”, the other “would drop out of the process” unless allowed to partner. p. 27: “first round indications of interest from 5 bidder groups” and “two other bidding groups”.
cells.What changes if answered differently: If the second partner was an eliminated or non-submitting party, one finalist (1 or 2) disappears silently. It would need an inferred Did not submit by 12/10, and the 2 eliminated or 9 non-submitters counts would fall by one.

cells.Question: Is Bidder 3’s 12/10 oral statement (valuation not above the ~$78 share price) a Bid, and which exit label fits?
cells.Recommended answer: Record no Bid: it is a valuation cap with no offer. Record Did not submit on 12/10, Exit reason Value at or below market price.
cells.Why, with page: p. 25: “their valuation would not be above the current stock price of approximately $78”; J.P. Morgan said it “was unlikely to be competitive and accordingly Bidder 3 did not submit a written offer.”
cells.What changes if answered differently: As a Bid, it gets an Informal row with Price high blank (the $78 is approximate) before the exit. If J.P. Morgan’s remark is read as exclusion, the label becomes Dropped by target.

cells.Question: Are the 15 NDA signers independent bidder units? The Buyer Group’s composition at the time of its IOI is also not stated.
cells.Recommended answer: Keep Count 15 and 9 non-submitters, with the caveat in the Notes.
cells.Why, with page: p. 23: the 24 financial contacts included “large suppliers of equity capital to lead buyers”. Annex A §5.2: confidentiality agreements with “certain of the Equity Investors” (plural). p. 16: BC Partners, Caisse, GIC and StepStone make up the Buyer Group. None of this says who signed which of the 15.
cells.What changes if answered differently: If several Buyer Group members signed separately, the 15 overstate independent units. cells.Question: Is the Buyer Group’s oral $82.50 on 12/12 Formal?
cells.Recommended answer: Formal. It answered the final-round request for improved bids and was backed by the group’s own merger agreement markup and committed financing.
cells.Why, with page: p. 26: “initially submitted an oral offer of $82.50 … working to increase the offer within the next few hours”; p. 25: final bid letters with revised merger agreements on 12/10.
cells.What changes if answered differently: As Informal, the Buyer Group’s price path would show a formal-to-informal step within the final round. That affects how the model reads intra-round revisions.

cells.Question: Industry Participant: 08/07 Bidder interest in round 0, then the 08/27 refusal of admission. Should it be treated as a participant who exited?
cells.Recommended answer: No. It never signed an NDA, bid or was admitted, so it gets no entry or exit; the refusal is an Other material event. Its spring 2014 talks go to Deal facts, because PetSmart was then exploring a combination or acquisition as buyer.
cells.Why, with page: p. 21: “merger with or acquisition of another participant in PetSmart’s industry”; p. 23: “Industry Participant would not be invited into the exploratory process”.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Treated as an entrant, it would add a strategic bidder to round 1 with a Dropped by target exit on 08/27. That changes the competition count and the strategic/financial mix.

cells.Question: Exit reason for the two IOI submitters eliminated on 11/03: Lower offer than rivals, or Would not improve earlier offer?
cells.Recommended answer: Lower offer than rivals. The target cut them at its $80.00 threshold, and their later statement that they would not go higher was not a response to a request to improve.
cells.Why, with page: p. 24: the board advanced bidders “at or above $80.00”; the eliminated parties then showed no “interest or ability to remain … above their respective initial indications”.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Would not improve earlier offer signals a firm valuation ceiling near the initial indication rather than a price below rivals.
